::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** May 8th [1894?]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Eton College, 2ALS to ATR
:::

Dear [Mrs Ritchie](people/person_1240.qmd)
How kind in you to write me such a pleasant letter. I like to know that the companions of my life have been beloved by other people. I had actually begun for my own pleasure another link in the Daisy Chain for the [Monthly Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd) but it was decided that it would weary the public.[^1]

I am much enjoying your [recollections](other_books/otherbook_698.qmd). I hope you have a great many more still to come.

I was sorry this morning to find that the so called [‘Sara Tytler’](people/person_802.qmd) is in so much need of  a pension. [Mr Besant](people/person_1652.qmd) is sending round a petition for her.[^2] It seems strange that she should never have been able to make more than a £162 a year, when everyone knew her name, and her books are always wholesome and often clever, though in awkward language.

But publishers are inscrutable! I have just seen a MSS full of ability, and by a practised hand rejected by the [publisher](organizations/other_230.qmd) of [Pretty Miss Smith](other_books/otherbook_699.qmd) where the uncle of an heiress tries to drive her out of her mind by letting owls loose in her bed room at night

However, I did not mean to write so much shop, only to say that if you are in these parts I should be delighted to see you and I am generally at home

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: This was *The Long Vacation*, a sequel to *The Daisy Chain*.
[^2]: Henrietta Keddie (1827-1914) was the author under the name 'Sarah Tytler' of more than seventy volumes of fiction, mainly for girls, from 1865;  she applied to the Royal Literary Fund five times between 1894 and 1913.
